notes: The parts list says 3 hook-up wires, but the circuit image shows 5 jumper wires: red (5V to + rail), black (GND to - rail), teal (pin 2 to button), orange (button leg to + rail) and a short black wire (resistor to - rail). I followed the image.

Button side 1 (legs 1.l/1.r) is placed in column 4 and side 2 (2.l/2.r) in column 6, straddling the centre gap. Column 4 goes to 5V through the orange wire. Column 6 goes to Arduino pin 2 through the teal wire and to the resistor.
The resistor runs from column 6 to column 9 on the lower half. Column 9 goes to the GND rail through the short black wire. This forms the pull-down.
The image shows the black GND wire on the second GND pin of the power header, so I used GND.2.

The catalogue puts rows a-e in the 't' bank and f-j in the 'b' bank. The image labels the halves the other way round. I mapped the upper half of the image to 't' and the lower half to 'b'. Exact row letters are arbitrary; only the column strips matter.
Rail hole numbers are estimated from the image. Red wire at bp.1, orange at bp.3, black GND wire at bn.1, short black wire at bn.7. The bottom rails are used: bp is the red + rail, bn is the - rail.
